title: Past Perfect (Pluscuamperfecto)
description: Describe actions that happened before another past action using había + past participle.

grammar.title: Past Perfect (Pretérito Pluscuamperfecto)
grammar.content:
The past perfect describes an action that happened BEFORE another past action. It's the 'past of the past.' You form it using the IMPERFECT of HABER + a past participle.

Imperfect of HABER:
- yo: había
- tú: habías
- él/ella/usted: había
- nosotros: habíamos
- vosotros: habíais
- ellos/ellas/ustedes: habían

Past participles:
- -AR → -ado (hablado)
- -ER → -ido (comido)
- -IR → -ido (vivido)
- Irregulars: hacer→hecho, decir→dicho, escribir→escrito, ver→visto, abrir→abierto, romper→roto, volver→vuelto, cubrir→cubierto
examples: Ya había comido cuando llegaste. (I had already eaten when you arrived.)
Nunca había visto algo tan bonito. (I had never seen anything so beautiful.)
Cuando llegué al cine, la película ya había empezado. (When I arrived at the cinema, the movie had already started.)
Ellos se habían ido antes de que yo llegara. (They had left before I arrived.)
grammar.aid_note: Romanian uses a similar structure: 'avusese' (had) + past participle. The Romanian past perfect (mai mult ca perfectul) is more complex with its own set of endings, but the concept is identical. The Spanish 'había + participle' is much simpler to conjugate.

pronunciation.title: Stress in Past Perfect Forms
pronunciation.content:
The imperfect of haber carries stress on the second-to-last syllable:

- había (ha-BÍ-a) — stress on the í
- habías (ha-BÍ-as) — stress on the í
- había (ha-BÍ-a) — stress on the í
- habíamos (ha-bí-A-mos) — stress on the á
- habíais (ha-bí-A-is) — stress on the á
- habían (ha-BÍ-an) — stress on the í

The accent marks on había/habías/habían show where the stress falls. The nosotros and vosotros forms have no accent because the stress falls naturally on the second-to-last syllable.
pronunciation.aid_note: Romanian stress patterns are similar — the auxiliary 'avuse' carries stress on the last syllable, but the concept of marking stress with accent marks is the same in both languages.

exercises.question: The past perfect is formed with:
exercises.explanation: The past perfect uses the IMPERFECT of haber (había, habías, había...) + past participle (hablado, comido, vivido).

exercises.question: Complete: 'Cuando llegué, ya ____ (comer).' (When I arrived, I had already eaten.)
exercises.explanation: 'Había comido' — past perfect: había + past participle comido.

exercises.question: What is the past participle of 'hacer'?
exercises.explanation: 'Hecho' is the irregular past participle of hacer. Used in past perfect: había hecho.

exercises.question: Complete: 'Ella ya ____ (salir) cuando yo llamé.' (She had already left when I called.)
exercises.explanation: 'Había salido' — past perfect of salir: había + past participle salido.

exercises.question: Complete: 'Ellos ya ____ (salir) cuando nosotros ____ (llegar).' (They had already left when we arrived.)
exercises.explanation: 'Habían salido' = past perfect (they had left). 'Llegamos' = preterite (we arrived). The past perfect action happened BEFORE the preterite action.

exercises.question: What is the past participle of 'decir'?
exercises.explanation: 'Dicho' is the irregular past participle of decir. Used in past perfect: había dicho (had said).
